candidates.name: ChicagoBoothML/DATA___InsideAirBnB
candidates.what_it_holds: Full Inside Airbnb per-city dumps committed directly to the repo for ~30 cities (Amsterdam, Austin, Barcelona, Berlin, Boston, Chicago, London, LA, Madrid, Melbourne, Montreal, Nashville, New Orleans, New York City, Oakland, Paris, Portland, San Diego, San Francisco, Santa Cruz, Seattle, Sydney, Toronto, Trentino, Venice, Vienna, Washington DC, etc). NYC folder contains listings.csv (4.7MB), listings.csv.gz (24MB), calendar.csv.gz (29.6MB), reviews.csv (6.8MB), reviews.csv.gz (62MB), neighbourhoods.csv, neighbourhoods.geojson -- a single full-scope vintage per city, no date in filenames. Repo created/pushed Dec 2015 (confirmed via repo metadata: created_at 2015-12-02, pushed_at 2015-12-03), so this is a ~2015 Inside Airbnb vintage, NOT the 2023-2024 Local Law 18 window. No license file (license: null).
candidates.why_useful: Not the target LL18 window, but it IS a genuine full-scope committed historical Inside Airbnb dump (listings+calendar+reviews) from ~2015 for NYC and 29 other cities -- older than anything on the current Inside Airbnb CDN and older than what we hold (Dec 2022+). Addresses gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps, pre-2023) as an 'older, longer' data point even though it misses the specific LL18 window; useful as a pre-period baseline for a 'listings before any STR regulation wave' comparison across many of our 13-city panel members (NYC, LA, Chicago, Austin, Nashville, New Orleans, San Diego, Paris, London, Barcelona, Sydney).
candidates.time_coverage: single vintage, ~Nov/Dec 2015 (pre-LL18, not the requested 2023-06→2024-03 window)
candidates.size_hint: NYC folder alone ~120MB across listings/calendar/reviews (compressed+uncompressed copies); repo-wide likely 1-2GB
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel in city coverage but is far older (2015 vs our Dec-2022+ coverage) -- not a duplicate, a genuinely older vintage.

candidates.name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/PostgreSQL+PostGIS scraper for Airbnb search-result pages (predates Inside Airbnb's own scraper; Tom Slee was an early independent Airbnb data researcher). No datasets are committed to the repo -- it is code only; users configure city bounding boxes and run it themselves against airbnb.com search pages. MIT licensed. Last meaningful activity ~2019 (v3.6); maintainer states it is no longer maintained and the Airbnb site structure has likely broken it since.
candidates.why_useful: Historically this project produced some of the earliest (pre-2015) multi-city Airbnb listing snapshots referenced in academic literature, potentially including NYC, but no such historical CSVs are committed in the current repo -- would require finding an archived release or a fork with data. Flagged as a method only; it scrapes airbnb.com directly, which is outside our sanctioned-source rule and should not be run without a human ToS decision.
candidates.geography: user-configurable, historically included major US/Canada/Europe cities
candidates.time_coverage: tool is undated; historical runs (not in this repo) reportedly go back to ~2012-2016

candidates.name: sangaline/wayback-machine-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Generic command-line Scrapy-based utility (and a maintained fork jan-kwiatkowski/wayback-machine-scraper) for crawling a domain's historical snapshots on the Internet Archive Wayback Machine and saving them to disk, by URL pattern and date range.
candidates.why_useful: Could, in principle, be pointed at archive.org's captures of insideairbnb.com/get-the-data.html or of the NYC OSE registration-law pages to recover download links/snapshots that predate the Inside Airbnb CDN's ~1-year retention window, filling the pre-2023 / LL18-window archive gap (#1) without touching airbnb.com itself. Not Airbnb-specific and not run by us in this pass -- pure tooling.
candidates.license: check repo (commonly MIT/BSD for these forks)
candidates.last_activity: actively forked; check individual fork dates

candidates.name: nycdb/nycdb
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source Python/Postgres tool that downloads and loads a large set of NYC housing/regulatory datasets (PLUTO parcel data, HPD violations, DOB permits, tax liens, rent stabilization rolls, evictions, etc.) into a local database with one command. Actively maintained (JustFix.nyc / housing data community project).
candidates.why_useful: Not Airbnb data itself, but a ready-made, one-command acquisition method for NYC housing/regulatory context (gap #13 housing/host-supply economics; possibly a path to NYC OSE short-term-rental registration counts if/when that dataset is added to its source list) -- useful as tooling to pull city registries around the LL18 period rather than as a direct Inside-Airbnb substitute.
candidates.time_coverage: current + historical NYC open-data extracts, varies by dataset
candidates.size_hint: n/a (pulls from NYC Open Data at run time)
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained as of recent GitHub search
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold the NYC OSE STR registry directly per CONTEXT.md; nycdb is a broader general-purpose NYC housing-data puller, not a duplicate of that specific dataset.

notes: Targeted search for GitHub repos specifically holding Inside Airbnb NYC snapshots dated 2023-06 through 2024-03 (the Local Law 18 registration/enforcement window) came up empty across 6 gh search repos calls (several queries returned zero results even though matching public repos plainly exist, suggesting gh search repos's free-text matching is stricter/AND-based on multi-word phrases -- single-keyword queries like 'inside-airbnb' and 'airbnb nyc data' did return hits) and ~7 WebSearch/WebFetch calls. The vast majority of GitHub 'Inside Airbnb NYC' repos are course/portfolio projects re-analyzing the single well-known Kaggle AB_NYC_2019.csv (2019 vintage) or the current Inside Airbnb CDN dump -- these were excluded per instructions as they add nothing new and do not touch the 2023-2024 window. No repo was found that specifically captured or mirrors the pre-enforcement (through Aug 2023) vs. post-enforcement (Sep 2023 on) NYC listing collapse (22,246 -> ~4,000 active listings, per press reporting) at the raw-data level. The one genuinely old committed archive found (ChicagoBoothML/DATA___InsideAirBnB, 2015 vintage) misses the target window by 8 years but is still a legitimate 'older than what we hold' data point for gap #1. Recommend: (a) a follow-up scout try GitHub code search (not repo search) for filename patterns like 'listings_2023-09' or 'nyc_ll18' with a fresh code-search budget; (b) a follow-up scout check whether the Internet Archive's own Wayback Machine (not GitHub) has cached insideairbnb.com data-page snapshots from mid-2023, which is a non-GitHub avenue outside this scout's modality; (c) academic replication packages (e.g. on OSF/Zenodo/Dataverse, not GitHub) studying the LL18 natural experiment are a more promising modality than GitHub repo search for this specific theme -- worth a dedicated scout on 'academic_replication' data_kind via Google Scholar / SSRN / Zenodo rather than gh search.
